analysis.is_complaint_reason: Customer reports losing £650 to a scam after paying by bank transfer and wants her money back, which indicates financial loss and dissatisfaction (CH-1).
analysis.summary: Customer [PERSON_1] paid a £650 deposit by bank transfer on 27/10 for a used car advertised on an online marketplace. The seller sent photos and a fake logbook and chatted on WhatsApp, then blocked her after payment. She reported it by phone on 30/10, says she shared no security details, and emailed WhatsApp screenshots. She wants her money back. This appears to be an authorised push payment scam and needs handover to Fraud & Scams.

timeline.event: Customer paid £650 deposit by bank transfer; seller later blocked her
Customer reported the scam by phone; WhatsApp screenshots emailed in

analysis.severity_reason: Suspected scam, which is High under CH-6, although the loss of £650 alone would be Medium.

vulnerability.suggested_support: None identified. Note 1 records no vulnerability and that the customer was asked. Keep alert for later indicators.

analysis.routing_reason: The customer was tricked into sending a payment to a fraudster, an APP scam, so the case must go to Fraud & Scams within 1 business day (ESC-1, FRD-2). Reimbursement is for the specialist to assess.

policy_citations.quote: the case must be handed to the Fraud & Scams team within 1 business day

handover.complaint_summary: Customer paid a £650 deposit by bank transfer on 27/10 for a used car found on an online marketplace. The seller used photos, a fake logbook and WhatsApp chat, then blocked her after payment. Suspected APP scam.

actions_taken: Scam reported by phone and logged on 30/10
handover.vulnerability_assessment: No indicators found. Note 1 records that the customer was asked.
handover.contact_preference: MISSING: the case holds a phone number and email token but no stated preference.
open_questions: Which account was the payment made from, and what were the payee details?
What was the exact time of the payment?
Were the card and online banking secured, and was this recorded?
Was the payee bank contacted to attempt recovery?
What is the contact preference and are any adjustments needed?
Which online marketplace was used, and has it been told?

fraud_details.fraudster_contact_method: Online marketplace listing, then WhatsApp chat

other_gaps: Screenshots are on file but the case does not say whether they have been reviewed.
The case does not say whether the customer reported it to the police or Action Fraud.
No evidence of the payment itself, such as a statement entry.
analysis.suggested_next_step: Hand over to Fraud & Scams within 1 business day of the 30/10 report. Check and record that the account is secured. Obtain payee details and the payment time. Do not promise reimbursement.
